responseMessageContents.text:
No problem. The backend supports 3 email providers — you don't need SendGrid. Here are your options:

## Email Provider Options (pick one)

| Option | Variables to set on Render | How to get it |
|--------|---------------------------|--------------|
| **Gmail** (easiest) | `GMAIL_OAUTH_TOKEN` | Use your existing Gmail account — create an OAuth token at Google Cloud Console |
| **AWS SES** | `IVX_SES_FROM_EMAIL` + `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` + `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | You already have AWS keys on GitHub secrets — just set the from-email |
| **SendGrid** | `SENDGRID_API_KEY` | You said you don't have this — skip it |

**Easiest path:** You already have AWS credentials in your GitHub secrets (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`). If you verify a sending email in AWS SES, you just need to set `IVX_SES_FROM_EMAIL` to that verified address on Render.

**Or Gmail:** If you use Gmail, you just need `GMAIL_OAUTH_TOKEN` (or `GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN`).

So your final Render variables are just:

| Variable | What |
|----------|------|
| `IVX_AI_GATEWAY_KEY` | Your Vercel AI Gateway key |
| `IVX_OWNER_PASSWORD` | Your owner login password |
| `IVX_SES_FROM_EMAIL` | A verified SES email address (you already have the AWS keys) |
| **Supabase** | Unpause project `kvclcdjmjghndxsngfzb` in Supabase dashboard |

That's it — 3 variables + unpause Supabase. Which email provider do you want to use?
